title: Are Feral Children Real?
summary: Josh and Chuck open with tour dates and a recollection of a bad live show at South by Southwest in Austin, then examine feral children: cases of children raised by animals or isolated from humans. They cover Ivan Mishchukov (Moscow dog boy), Amala and Kamala (debunked wolf girls of India), Oksana Malaya (Ukrainian dog girl), Peter the Wild Boy (18th-century Hanover and London), Jean de Liège, Memmie Le Blanc, Genie, Misha Defonseca's fabricated memoir, and Marina Chapman. They discuss the three categories (isolated, confined, raised among animals), critical period for language acquisition, and skepticism that many stories were fraud or misdiagnosed developmental disabilities such as Bruno Bettelheim's theory and Pitt-Hopkins syndrome. The episode ends with a listener email from a self-described chronic pot user in Texas and sign-off information.

segments.title: Tour dates and South by Southwest bad show
segments.summary: Hosts announce 2018 tour dates, then recall a poorly run live podcast at South by Southwest in Austin held in a noisy bar.

segments.title: Ivan Mishukov, the Moscow dog boy
segments.summary: Ivan Mishukov, a six-year-old street child in late-1990s Moscow, lived among a pack of stray dogs that took him in until social workers removed him to a group home.

segments.title: Definition of feral children and categories
segments.summary: Discussion of historical feral child legends such as Romulus and Remus, Linnaeus's Homo ferus, and three categories: isolated, confined, and raised among animals, with examples like Emi Yati and Wang Shuangfeng.

segments.title: Genie and isolated feral children
segments.summary: Genie was kept confined in a closet from age two to twelve and developed a feral nature, which the hosts contrast with children raised by animals.

segments.title: Feral children as natural laboratory and animal-like traits
segments.summary: Feral children offer a window on language acquisition and nature versus nurture, since unethical experiments are impossible. Reported animal-like behaviors include barking, running on all fours, raw meat eating, and keen senses, with John of Liège as an example.

segments.title: Fraud and misdiagnosis in feral child stories
segments.summary: Many fantastic stories are doubted; J.A.L. Singh's wolf girls Amala and Kamala were revealed as children with developmental defects, and Misha Defonseca's wolf-raised memoir was fabricated. Marina Chapman's monkey story is poorly documented.

segments.title: Peter the Wild Boy
segments.summary: Peter, a feral boy found in 1725 in the Hertzwold forest near Hamelin, was brought to King George in Hanover, then to London, and later lived on a farm on a pension until his death in 1785; historian Lucy Worsley suggested Pitt-Hopkins syndrome.

segments.title: Oksana Malaya, Ukrainian dog girl, and critical period
segments.summary: Oksana Malaya was raised by dogs on a Ukrainian farm for about five years after her parents left her outside. Found and later socialized, she showed dog-like behavior and partial language recovery, which supports the critical period theory. Bruno Bettelheim's autism theory is discussed and found insufficient; Memmie Le Blanc is cited as a non-impaired case.

segments.title: Listener email from a Texas pot smoker
segments.summary: An anonymous listener describes daily marijuana use and driving while stoned, and says he views it as a legal-status issue; the hosts respond.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact info
segments.summary: Hosts give social media, email and website contact information and close the episode.
